question.title: NEP 55 — Add a UTF-8 Variable-Width String DType to NumPy

caller.text: NumPy users and downstream libraries currently using object string arrays, including Pandas, scikit-learn, h5py and PyTables.

input.text: N-dimensional arrays or array-like data of arbitrarily sized Python strings; optional user-provided missing sentinel and coerce flag; numeric/other inputs may be converted to strings by default or rejected in strict mode.

output.text: A first-class NumPy StringDType array backed by variable-width UTF-8 storage, yielding Python str scalars and supporting mutations, vector operations and serialization with the specified missing-data behavior.

limits.text: Do not change ordinary dtype inference for strings; no new built-in missing sentinel, unknown-encoding memory-map dtype, generic bytes fix or fast SIMD string implementation is required.

Target integration is NumPy 2.0 but the new DType and file format can slip to 2.1. The initial external prototype requires NUMPY_EXPERIMENTAL_DTYPE_API. These are initial proposal constraints, not current-environment claims.
Python buffer protocol and idiomatic Cython typed memoryviews are explicitly unsupported for this layout without future changes.

source_positions.section: Cython Support and the Buffer Protocol

limits.text: Small-string optimization, a 32-bit length field and the exact np.strings rename are alternatives or future optimizations, not mandatory gates. Locale-aware ordering, case folding and normalization are future work.
Preliminary prototype benchmark numbers are reported by the author; they do not define a required speedup. Arbitrary missing sentinels may require holding the GIL while sorting.

whole_must.predicate: Provide a first-class NumPy variable-width UTF-8 string DType with no per-array maximum string-length parameter and Python str scalar behavior, while leaving ordinary string inference unchanged.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Construct a multidimensional array containing "a", "é" and a much longer later element, then extract an item. Truncation, an object-only container, fixed maximum width, or changing np.array(["a"]) inference falsifies full integration.

whole_must.predicate: Support default non-string-to-string coercion and a coerce=False mode that rejects non-string data during array creation.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Create StringDType(coerce=False) from ["x", 7]. Silently stringifying 7, or requiring a separate caller validation pass because the DType does not enforce the rule, falsifies this contract.

whole_must.predicate: Accept user-provided missing sentinels with the proposed categories: NaN-like propagation and sorting-last behavior, string sentinels treated as strings, and errors for unsupported-object comparisons.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Create an array with na_object=np.nan and add/sort it; losing the sentinel or sorting it as an ordinary string fails. With na_object=None, silently comparing/sorting it as a string also fails.

whole_must.predicate: Provide datatype-managed variable-width UTF-8 storage and a supported C interface for allocation, copying and freeing, so downstream code can use string-array data without reducing it to generic Python-object references.

source_positions.section: Memory layout and Managing Heap Allocations

whole_must.falsifying_input: A downstream C operation needs supported access to the typed string buffers. A generic Python-object array with no datatype-managed string storage or C allocation/access interface fails; a safe alternative allocator is not excluded solely for its layout.

whole_must.predicate: Support in-place string mutation, including length growth, without data races or use-after-free within the advertised concurrent-access contract.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Enlarge a string while another thread accesses it under the implementation's documented supported concurrency contract. A use-after-free or data race, or forbidding all element mutation, fails the outcome; a different safe synchronization scheme does not.

whole_must.predicate: Provide round-trip casts to built-in dtypes, comparisons in Unicode-code-point order, string add, string/integer multiply, isnan, and rejection of binary operations between unequal StringDType parameterizations.

source_positions.section: Casts, ufunc support, and string manipulation functions

whole_must.falsifying_input: Concatenate two string arrays or call isnan on a NaN sentinel; absent ufunc dispatch fails. Combining unequal na_object/coerce descriptors without the specified error also fails.

whole_must.predicate: Support lossless NumPy npy/npz serialization of variable-width string data without requiring pickle, and support pickling/unpickling when requested.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Save/reload a variable-width string array with long and non-ASCII elements under allow_pickle=False. Refusal or string loss fails; a supported safe format encoding need not use the exact initially proposed version-4 sidecar header.

whole_must.predicate: Integrate the new DType with supported NumPy array functionality and string manipulation operations, including advanced indexing and the Python/C DType interfaces.

source_positions.section: Usage and Impact; Python API; Implementation

whole_must.falsifying_input: Apply advanced indexing and a string uppercase operation to a multidimensional StringDType array. A standalone one-dimensional string store that cannot participate in NumPy indexing/ufunc behavior fails this subsystem requirement.

partial_must.predicate: Construct a NumPy array of variable-width UTF-8 strings of unequal lengths without a maximum-length scan or truncation, retaining the first-class string dtype.

source_positions.section: Problems with Fixed-Width Strings; Python API

partial_must.falsifying_input: Construct ["a", "é", "a much longer string"]. A fixed-width truncated result, a required maximum-width scan, or a generic Python list fails the partial storage/construction purpose.

partial_must.predicate: In strict mode reject non-string inputs during construction rather than silently coercing them or requiring a second caller-side validation pass.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Pass ["ok", 42] with coerce=False. A successful array containing "42" falsifies strict validation.

partial_must.predicate: Return a NumPy array that supports its ordinary shape/indexing use and produces Python string scalars; a foreign scalar or one-dimensional-only container is not this output.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Construct a 2-by-2 string array and select a scalar element. A foreign table-column object lacking NumPy array shape/indexing is insufficient.

question.independent_partial_purpose: Load and validate heterogeneous-length UTF-8 text into a typed NumPy array in one construction pass. This immediately replaces an object-array sanitization pass even before the entire allocator, missing-data matrix, serialization and string namespace migration are finished.
question.remaining_adapter: Select/import the provided dtype, pass coerce=False and translate an existing array-like input boundary. Full first-design work still includes all sentinel semantics, arena/C interfaces, thread-safe mutation, casts/ufuncs and npy/npz sidecar serialization. If the adapter must implement variable-width storage or strict validation itself, partial completion is not established.
question.same_name_wrong_actor_output_failure: Pandas StringDtype, an Apache Arrow string column, a TensorFlow RaggedTensor or a fixed-width NumPy Unicode dtype may share string terminology, but the partial action requires a multidimensional typed NumPy array with strict construction semantics. Converting such a foreign object to a generic object array is not the requested output.

candidates.name: NumPy StringDType
candidates.proposed_use: Construct typed NumPy arrays of variable-width UTF-8 text with constructor-enforced strict validation; use the documented allocator-mediated C interface for downstream string access and replacement.
